title: Amul Raises Milk Prices by Up to Rs 4 a Litre, Second Hike in Six Months
excerpt: GCMMF cites fodder, feed, packaging and fuel costs plus uneven rainfall for the November 12 increase. Taaza rises ₹2 a litre, Gold ₹4, and Mother Dairy has moved in step.
body:
• Amul has raised fresh pouch milk prices by ₹2-4 per litre across India from November 12, its second increase in six months.
  • Amul Taaza toned milk (3% fat) rises ₹2 per litre, a 3.3% increase; Amul Gold full-cream milk (6% fat) rises ₹4 per litre, up 5.5%.
  • GCMMF blames a steep rise in production and processing costs — fodder, cattle feed ingredients, packaging film and fuel — compounded by low, uneven rainfall.
  • Mother Dairy has matched the move with its own ₹2-4 per litre increase from November 12, so most urban households will pay more whichever brand they buy.

India's largest dairy cooperative has made the morning milk run more expensive for the second time in six months. The Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF), which markets milk under the Amul brand, raised fresh pouch milk prices by ₹2-4 per litre across major variants and packs in markets across India from November 12, an increase of roughly 4-5%, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. The revision follows a ₹2 per litre increase announced on May 13.

What each variant costs now

The price of Amul Taaza toned milk, the cooperative's largest-selling variant with 3% milk fat, has been increased by ₹2 per litre, or 3.3%. Amul Gold milk, with 6% milk fat, will cost ₹4 more per litre, a 5.5% increase. The increases apply across major milk-selling variants and pack sizes, GCMMF said.

Why prices are rising

GCMMF attributed the increase to a steep rise in the input costs of milk production and processing over the past year: green and dry fodder, cattle feed ingredients such as oil cake, maize and molasses, milk packaging film, and fuel. It also cited low and uneven rainfall in Gujarat and several other parts of the country. "In the current challenging environmental circumstances due to low and uneven rainfall in Gujarat as well as many parts of India, we are constrained to increase the consumer price of milk to pay better prices to our producers and support them in these difficult times," the federation said in its statement.

"We are constrained to increase the consumer price of milk to pay better prices to our producers and support them in these difficult times."

— Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF)

Where the money goes

The federation said its member unions had already raised the procurement prices paid to farmers by 4-5% over the past year, and that a further revision would follow. Around 80% of the revenue collected from consumers through the Amul cooperative network is returned to its 36 lakh milk producers, GCMMF said, adding that a major portion of the latest increase will go back to producers.

Not just Amul

Mother Dairy announced a similar increase of ₹2-4 per litre across its liquid milk variants, also effective November 12, particularly in the Delhi-NCR market, according to BizzBuzz. With the country's two largest liquid-milk brands moving together, the increase lands directly on monthly household food budgets — for diaspora families tracking the cost of living back home, milk is the most visible daily-price signal of food inflation in India.
